name: Thusharagiri Waterfalls
tagline: Three spray‑filled falls and accessible forest treks in the Western Ghats
summary: A cluster of three waterfalls (Thumbithullumpara, Mazhavil Chattam, Erattumukku) set in the Western Ghats near Kodanchery. Well suited to short treks and scenic walks after the monsoon (Oct–Feb).
description: Thusharagiri is a band of three waterfalls on the Chalippuzha stream in Kozhikode district. Two hill streams join and split here, creating spray-filled cascades and forested trekking routes.
The site matters for nature lovers and light trekkers: trails wind through evergreen hill forest, there are natural pools and multiple viewpoints, and the falls create dramatic post-monsoon scenery.

Visitors get short, well-marked treks (many are run under the forest department/eco‑tourism programme), photographic viewpoints, and a rustic eco‑tourism centre. Some falls sit inside managed forest zones so access, timings and guides are controlled seasonally.
Thusharagiri makes a compact day trip from Kozhikode and pairs well with nearby hill stops such as Areeppara and Chembukadavu.
highlights: Three main falls (Thenpara/Thenpara/Thenpara highest, Thumbithullumpara, Mazhavil Chattam and Erattumukku) and multiple viewpoints
Short treks and easy hikes through evergreen Western Ghats forest
Best post-monsoon colours and steady flow from October into winter
Forest‑department eco‑tourism management with ticketing and guided routes
1.5 km forest walk from the eco‑tourism ticket counter to Thumbithullumpara (scenic trail)

sections.heading: Background
body: Thusharagiri (literally ‘snow‑capped peak’) takes its name from the white spray of the falls. Two hill streams meet to form the Chalippuzha river and split into a series of cascades and pools set in low‑elevation Western Ghats forest.
The site is a long‑standing local eco‑tourism spot managed by the Kerala Forest Department and featured on Kerala Tourism and district tourism pages as a waterfall + trekking destination.

sections.heading: What to see and do
body: Short, photo‑friendly treks take you to Thumbithullumpara and Mazhavil Chattam; Erattumukku is visible from near the parking/approach. Trails are mostly graded for light to moderate walkers rather than technical climbers.

Bring a camera and sturdy shoes—views, river crossings on log bridges and mossy boulders make for classic Western Ghats shots. Avoid swimming near strong currents; there are natural pools but currents and rocks make some spots unsafe.

sections.heading: Plan your visit
body: Location and distance: Thusharagiri sits in the Kodanchery / Nellipoyil area, about 50–54 km from Kozhikode town. Approach is usually by road to the Thusharagiri eco‑tourism centre; local directions use Kodanchery / Chembukadavu as reference points.

Timings and tickets: The Kerala Forest Department runs ticketing and guided access for the forest trails. As of Jan 7, 2026 the forest department allowed access to Thumbithullumpara and Mazhavil Chattam from 08:30–15:00 daily (eco‑tourism rules apply) and reported an entry fee of ₹40 for Indian adults (children and foreign rates listed by the department). Confirm opening hours and fees at the local ticket counter before travel.

Best time: Visit after the southwest monsoon—October through February—when trails dry quickly, flows are scenic and the weather is cool. Heavy monsoon months (June–September) bring strong flows and restricted access.

sections.heading: Safety, permits and local rules
body: Follow the forest department and eco‑tourism guide instructions. Certain falls and routes (for example Thonikkayam, Avinjithode and some inner‑forest trails) are seasonally closed for safety and wildlife reasons.

Carry water, wear grippy footwear, avoid stepping on wet boulders, and do not attempt unmarked routes. Confirm live access and hiring of authorised guides at the Thusharagiri ticket/eco‑centre before setting out.

latest.text: Forest department reopens Thumbithullumpara and Mazhavil Chattam to visitors after monsoon restrictions; access allowed 08:30–15:00 and entry fee reported ₹40 for Indian adults.
Kerala Forest Department ecotourism listing records Thusharagiri as a managed waterfall‑trek destination and publishes entrance and trekking programme charges (department tariff document).

visitorInfo.bestTime: October to February (post-monsoon into early winter)
visitorInfo.howToReach: About 50–54 km east of Kozhikode (Kozhikode → Thamarassery → Kodancherry/Nellipoyil). Park at the Thusharagiri eco‑tourism centre and walk the forest trail (roughly 1.5 km) to Thumbithullumpara viewpoint.
etiquette: Buy tickets and check permitted trails at the Thusharagiri eco‑tourism counter; follow forest guides.
Wear sturdy, non‑slip shoes; many paths are rocky and can be slippery after rain.
Avoid visiting during heavy monsoon (June–September); check current access times (some falls open only 08:30–15:00).
Do not enter closed areas; respect wildlife and leave no trash.
